findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. A membership has a single role, so this is either always false (if the helpers check ADMIN and OWNER exclusively) or true only for owners (if isTeamAdmin already treats OWNER as admin). Team admins who are not the booking host and not an attendee are rejected with FORBIDDEN, even though the flag is named and used as an admin-or-owner grant and the bookings UI treats team admins/owners as managers. They cannot add guests to team bookings they otherwise manage. This should be ||, and it should not query team id 0 when eventType.teamId is null.

findings.title: Cancelled, past, and no-guest events still accept new guests
findings.body: After the permission check the handler never reads booking status, endTime, or eventType.disableGuests before inserting attendees and emailing invites. Any logged-in attendee (not only the host) may call this with a numeric booking id. disableGuests is on the included event type and is ignored, so a host who turned guests off can still have arbitrary addresses emailed a CONFIRMED invite that includes the video URL and meeting password from the booking references. The same path runs for CANCELLED, REJECTED, and PENDING bookings, and for meetings that already ended. The new ICS builders hardcode status CONFIRMED. The bookings menu also offers this action for past confirmed rows (BookingListItem bookedActions, rendered around line 554), so this is not only a raw-API issue. Reject anything that is not an upcoming accepted booking, and honor disableGuests.

findings.title: Seated events are not capacity-checked and get no seat rows
findings.body: createMany inserts plain Attendee rows and later copies seatsPerTimeSlot onto the calendar payload, but never compares current attendees plus new guests to seatsPerTimeSlot and never creates the per-attendee seat rows (reference UIDs) seated bookings use. Occupancy, the seats UI, and seat-scoped cancel/reschedule links will not include these people. Depending on whether availability counts attendees or seats, the slot is either overfilled with people who still have the meeting link, or marked full without usable seat records. Paid-per-seat events also skip payment for these extra people. Block this mutation when seatsPerTimeSlot is set, or add real seats through the seat booking path and enforce the cap.

findings.title: Attendee insert is not rolled back if calendar sync fails
findings.body: prisma.booking.update createMany commits the new attendees before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, with no transaction and no compensating delete. If the calendar call throws (revoked credential, provider error, or the wrong user's credentials), the mutation fails but the rows remain. A retry then filters those emails out as already attending and throws BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the caller cannot finish calendar sync or notifications. The host sees an error while the booking already lists the guests, and the guests were never emailed because sendAddGuestsEmails runs only after the calendar call. Persist guests only after sync succeeds, or roll the insert back on failure.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the host's
findings.body: EventManager is constructed from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), not from the booking host. The query already loads booking.user.credentials and never uses them. Calendar references on the booking are stored against the host credential. Attendees are explicitly allowed to call this mutation, and the team-owner branch is meant to allow non-hosts; those callers do not have the host credential, so updateCalendarAttendees cannot update the host event. It will throw (leaving the rows committed with no rollback) or skip. Either way the host calendar, and Meet/Zoom guest lists derived from it, do not gain the new guests. Build EventManager from the booking owner (and that user's calendar credentials), including co-host credentials for collective events.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and racy
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but the filter uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) without lowercasing or trimming guest, and split(',') does not trim entries. Blocked@example.com bypasses blocked@example.com, and a space after a comma in the env var bypasses that entry. The same === comparison against existing attendees is case-sensitive, the input array is not deduped, and the organizer address is not excluded, so one request can createMany both a@x.com and A@x.com, the same address twice, or the host as their own guest. There is no unique (bookingId, email) constraint and the check-then-insert is not locked, so two concurrent calls can also insert the same guest twice. Duplicate rows break the attendee list and send duplicate invites. When every address is filtered, the error key emails_must_be_unique_valid is also used for blacklist hits, so the client shows 'Emails must be unique and valid' instead of a blocked-email error. If at least one address remains, dropped addresses are silent and the UI still toasts success.

findings.title: Notifications use the raw address list and hide send failures
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests array, not the filtered uniqueGuests that were actually inserted. In email-manager, newGuests.includes(attendee.email) is what chooses AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new ICS REQUEST) versus the guests-added notice. The dialog only receives bookingId, so a user can retype an existing attendee plus a new address; the existing attendee is skipped in the DB but still matches newGuests and gets a fresh booking-confirmation invite, which can duplicate the event on their calendar. evt.team is never set (the query does not even load eventType.team or hosts), so the team-member loop in sendAddGuestsEmails is dead and collective/round-robin co-hosts are not notified. Send failures are caught, logged as a fixed string without the error, and the mutation still returns success, so the UI shows 'Guests added' when nobody was emailed.

findings.title: Add-guest emails ignore event-type email opt-out
findings.body: Every other sender in this file checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail before sending. sendAddGuestsEmails does not take event-type metadata and always emails the organizer, every existing attendee, and each new guest, including full calendar invites. Event types with standard emails disabled still emit these messages when a guest is added. The handler has booking.eventType loaded and should pass its metadata so the same opt-out applies.

findings.title: One occurrence is updated but the event is marked recurring
findings.body: The handler updates only the given bookingId, but evt.recurringEvent is set from booking.eventType.recurringEvent for every instance of a recurring type. That field is what scheduled emails and calendar updates use to treat a CalendarEvent as a series (RRULE / series update). The recurring tab hides this action, so it is used on a single upcoming occurrence, yet the invite and calendar payload still describe the whole series. A guest is then on every occurrence in Google/Outlook (or holds an RRULE invite) while only one Booking row lists them, so later instances disagree between Cal.com and the external calendar. Either omit recurringEvent and target that occurrence's calendar reference, or add the guest to every future booking in the recurringEventId group and update the series once.

findings.title: New guests are stored with an empty name
findings.body: guestsFullDetails sets name to an empty string for every new guest. New guests are emailed via AttendeeScheduledEmail, which addresses them as `${name} <${email}>`, so the To header is ' <guest@example.com>'. Some mailers reject or blank that address, and calendar attendees are created with an empty display name. OrganizerAddGuestsEmail also interpolates attendees[0].name into the subject with no fallback (organizer-add-guests-email.ts line 28), so a blank first attendee yields 'with ' and no name. Store the email (or its local part) as the name when the guest did not provide one.

findings.title: Guest list has no upper bound
findings.body: guests is an unbounded z.array of emails, and MultiEmail can append fields without a cap. Any authenticated host or attendee can submit thousands of addresses in one call. The handler insert them and fans out a calendar invite per address containing the meeting URL. OrganizerAddGuestsEmail also puts every attendee email in replyTo, so a large list can exceed header limits and fail the send after the rows are already committed. Cap and dedupe the array in the schema before any writes or sends.

findings.title: No tests for add-guests authorization or side effects
findings.body: The new mutation ships with no handler or UI tests. Permission (admin vs owner vs attendee vs stranger), blacklist and case-variant duplicates, cancelled and seated bookings, the single-occurrence recurring case, and calendar or email failure after the insert are all untested, so the authorization, seat, and rollback bugs above would not be caught in CI.
